chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Al-Husayn ibn Saeed, from Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, who said:
I asked Abu Abdullah (peace be upon him) about the slaughter of the eunuch, so he (peace be upon him) said: There is no problem.

key_terms.الْخَصِيِّ: The eunuch (a male who has been castrated)
key_terms.ذَبِيحَة: Slaughter (ritual killing of an animal for food)
key_terms.لَا بَأْسَ: There is no problem (a legal phrase indicating permissibility or validity)

ai.seo_question: Is the ritual slaughter performed by a eunuch considered valid in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: In this narration from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (AS) validates the ritual slaughter (*dhabihah*) performed by a eunuch (*khass*), affirming its legal acceptability for consumption. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it clarifies that the physical absence of male reproductive organs does not invalidate the essential conditions of slaughter, distinguishing it from cases where the slaughterer lacks sanity or maturity. The chain of transmission highlights the reliability of Ibrahim ibn Abi al-Bilad, a prominent companion of the Imams, in transmitting these practical legal details.
